Opened the Legimi ebook sample and verified first-person autobiographical narration across the opening chapters.
Opened the Project Gutenberg Australia plain-text edition and checked the opening, Chapters 10, 20, 23, and 34, and the ending for continued first-person narration.

Searched specifically for “Emily Blair” with narrator, “tells her own story,” “Emily's first-person,” and “first-person POV”; Kirkus and a 1942 Kitchen-Klatter review independently described Emily as telling the story herself.
Film pages and adaptation synopses were inspected as discovery results but were not used because their third-person plot-summary grammar does not establish the novel's narrative person.
No credible source indicated alternating, second-person, or third-person base narration.
person_note: The base narrator is protagonist Emily Blair, who retrospectively writes her own life story in first person. The diagnostic Goodreads passages repeatedly expose Emily's participating “I,” while the gnomic quotations use generic “we” or “you” and were not treated as person evidence. A complete library text confirms the same narrator from the opening through multiple interior chapters and the ending, and independent contemporary reviews explicitly say that Emily tells the story herself. No sustained section in another person was found; the only minor limitation is that several supplied quotes are aphoristic rather than narratively diagnostic.
